Koel was 14 months when she joined Da Vinci in the Toddler Class. 3 months ago, some of the students in Koel's class moved onto the Primary section. This also meant that several young kids now came to her class, and my little girl who once was a baby of the class transformed into the big sister. One day, as I was waiting to receive her, I was narrated a very sweet story by her teacher which touched my heart to the deepest levels.

As was informed, when the younger kids wanted something in class, Koel was the first one to notice, and she would stop whatever activity she was doing, to help the young child. One day, a young toddler was thirsty and made a gesture for the same. Koel noticed this from the other end of the class and ran to pour a glass of water for him. After sometime the young tod was thirsty again but instead of figuring what to do, he immediately went to look for Koel and asked her to pour him another glass of water.

Why I chose to share this story is because it very  beautifully depicts the empathy of the elder child and the independence of the younger one which all blossomed with their simple interaction in class. While the curriculum covers the knowledge aspect, it is these interactions of a mixed age classroom that really transform these young children into independent and caring humans.

When Krrish joined DVM, he was 4.5 years old and we were returning from a post COVID era. If COVID was tough on us, it was worse with the kids who lost their sense of social being. Even while being a Montessori curriculum, the children are exposed to a variety of activities on par with international schools, such as Art, Speech and Drama, Physical Fitness, Capoeira, Spanish Music, in the Elementary classroom, and Music, Art, Fitness and Yoga in the Primary and Toddler classrooms.

The head of the school, Ms. Ashani, is deeply invested in ensuring that while the kids continue to learn from the Montessori classroom their future is safeguarded too, hence working on several tie ups with prominent big schools and introducing kids to a variety of inter school activities. The sincerity runs top down and the love, concern and nurturing can be seen in all members of the school from the administrator to each of the teachers in the Toddler, Primary and Elemnentary classroom, as well as the Didis!

I couldn't have asked for a better school for my kids! Thank you for making us a part of the DVM family!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Terrible experience. The staff was so unwelcoming.

We had booked an orientation - we reached around 10-15 minutes late, because or which they informed us that we wouldn’t be able to see the school as it had already started - which i completely respect and understand. O asked them if we should come another day, to which she said that they would at least have the scheduled interaction.

However the interaction with the faculty was so superficial. The conversation started with a breakdown of the fee details, as opposed to talking about the school facility, pedagogy, and faculty - which other places did. I asked a few questions which they were completely disinterested in answering. I asked them how a Playway curriculum compares to a Montessori - their response was “You’ll have to do your own research”. If i was an educator myself, would I seriously come to you? A few other questions about timings etc, all they said “It’s on the website”. As a parent, are we not entitled to ask such questions?

A preschool is technically a child’s first foray into a structured academic set up, and it’s so important the place feel warm and welcoming. If i as a parent felt so judged and unwelcome, I can only imagine what it would feel like for my child to attend here.

I must stress that this was sooooo different from all the other preschools (I’ve checked out most preschools in South & Central Mumbai). At all the other places, they wanted to know about parents’ education, profession, their parenting philosophy, environment at home etc. The other schools also made so much effort on talking about their school and what they do.

Just for the record, we are a business family based in South Bombay - and by all means I would put us in the category of well-educated, affluent individuals who can clearly afford the fees. I would’ve so much happy had the school tried understanding us as and our child as individuals instead of constantly judging us.

Sharing my individual experience here. O understand some people have truly had a good experience for their kids here, so sincerely happy for them.
